title: Sometimes
subtitle: Sometimes 表示『有時／間中』，但不同近義詞會改變頻率、語域和事件模式。 有些表達偏低頻（occasionally, once in a while），有些強調隔一段時間再
description: Sometimes 表示『有時／間中』，但不同近義詞會改變頻率、語域和事件模式。 有些表達偏低頻（occasionally, once in a while），有些強調隔一段時間再發生（from time to time, every so often），有些偏口語（now and then），而 sporadically 更進一步表示零星、無規律。

options.explanation: Occasionally ✓ — means from time to time but not often. Here, the event happens, but not often. The frequency, register and pattern all fit Occasionally better than the other choices.

At times — means on some occasions, often when describing a state or condition. This works well for states or qualities that are true on some occasions, but it is less natural for the lower-frequency or interval-based pattern tested here. The decisive clue is that the event happens, but not often.

From time to time — means occasionally over a period, often with repeated but infrequent occurrence. This suggests recurrence over a period and is less suitable when the sentence is purely conversational or describes a temporary state. The decisive clue is that the event happens, but not often.

Often — means frequently and is stronger than sometimes. This raises the frequency too much; the sentence does not say the event is frequent. The decisive clue is that the event happens, but not often.

Usually — means in most cases or as the normal pattern. This changes the meaning substantially because it says the event is the normal or majority pattern. The decisive clue is that the event happens, but not often.

Rarely — means not often and is generally less frequent than sometimes. This lowers the frequency too far and suggests the event is exceptional. The decisive clue is that the event happens, but not often.
